newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fifteen children feared dead after South African rains.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen children feared dead after South African rains.

text.p: A truck carrying 15 school children was washed away in a raging river in South Africa's Eastern Cape province after the wettest November yet in parts of the region, police said on Thursday.

Senior Police Superintendent John Best told state radio the tragedy occurred on Monday when the truck driver tried to cross over a low-lying bridge on the Sand River near the town of Patensie. The body of one child was found on Thursday afternoon.
Best said efforts to recover the other bodies were hampered by inaccessible terrain. A police helicopter was also grounded because of poor visibility in the continuing rains.
A month of steady rainfall in the Eastern Cape has prompted weather officials to issue flood warnings in some districts.
In Port Elizabeth, the province's largest city, a total of 213 mm of rain has fallen so far this month, beating the previous record of 200 mm measured for the month in 1955.
More than 65 mm of rain has fallen over the city since Wednesday alone, and the weather office has forecast heavy showers for Thursday night and Friday.

Unless the rains abate, city rescue workers as well as the police and defence force have said they will evacuate residents from Port Elizabeth's shack areas of Kleinskool, Soweto-on-Sea and Veeplaas, who are under threat by the rising Chatty River.
City officials said the homeless would be housed in community halls.
